score.scoring_notes: High alignment and feasibility for native assimilation; moderate security/ecosystem risks due to limited verified information; licensing clarity unknown pending human review.

recommendation.rationale_summary: Based on the observed characteristics of tools in this class, ruflo appears to center on declarative workflow/dataflow orchestration with resilient execution. Rather than adopting a new runtime or creating a dependency, MITIGATE can assimilate the most valuable patterns natively (declarative flow specs, DAG scheduling, retries/backoff, artifact/lineage hooks) while preserving the existing core and maintaining provider independence.

assumptions_and_limits.information_source_limitations: This evaluation is based on technology watcher observations and common patterns for similarly named workflow/dataflow systems. No external networks were accessed and ruflo was not installed, activated, or executed.
unknowns_to_confirm: Exact primary domain and scope of ruflo (workflow, dataflow, job orchestration, or adjacent)
License type and obligations (OSI-approved?, copyleft?, usage constraints)
Security model: RBAC, multi-tenancy isolation, secret handling, provenance, plugin trust model
Operational model: deployment topologies, persistence requirements, scaling constraints
Extensibility: plugin API stability, SDK maturity, backward compatibility guarantees

capabilities.summary: Ruflo is treated as a member of the workflow/dataflow orchestration class. Capabilities below are framed as typical for that class and must be verified before any adoption steps.

reported_or_typical.name: Declarative workflow specs
reported_or_typical.description: Define multi-step flows as DAGs using a DSL (YAML/JSON/py-DSL)

reported_or_typical.name: Distributed worker execution
reported_or_typical.description: Pool of workers executing tasks with leases/heartbeats

reported_or_typical.name: Retries and backoff policies
reported_or_typical.description: Configurable retry strategies per step with jitter/backoff

reported_or_typical.name: Caching/artifacts
reported_or_typical.description: Optional step outputs caching and artifact management

reported_or_typical.name: Observability hooks
reported_or_typical.description: Run logs, metrics, traces, lineage hooks

useful_architectural_patterns.why_useful: Separation of flow intent from execution enables policy checks, reproducibility, and static validation.
useful_architectural_patterns.native_assimilation: Introduce a small, versioned FlowSpec (JSON Schema) compiled to existing MITIGATE job primitives.

useful_architectural_patterns.why_useful: Heartbeats and leases prevent duplicate execution and enable safe failover.
useful_architectural_patterns.native_assimilation: Use existing queue/executor with per-task leases and heartbeat TTL; store state in MITIGATE's persistence layer.

useful_architectural_patterns.why_useful: Reduces blast radius and improves resilience under transient faults.
useful_architectural_patterns.native_assimilation: Add per-step policies (max_retries, backoff, jitter) and enforce idempotency keys at dispatch.

useful_architectural_patterns.why_useful: Security and governance enforcement before runs start.
useful_architectural_patterns.native_assimilation: Route FlowSpec through Policy Engine; deny/alter runs failing org policies.

useful_architectural_patterns.why_useful: Integrates flows into broader platform events.
useful_architectural_patterns.native_assimilation: Subscribe to platform event bus; map events to FlowSpec triggers with filters and rate limits.
Emit standardized lineage and artifact metadata to Audit/Observability subsystems.

observed_or_inferred_existing_capabiliti: Python-first services and tooling (repository composition suggests Python 3.x)
Strong documentation and technology evaluation process
Security-conscious workflows and policy enforcement emphasis
potential_overlaps: Existing policy engine and secrets management
gaps_ruflo_like_capabilities_might_fill: Built-in DAG validation (cycles, fan-out limits, resource guards)
overlap_with_mitigate.notes: Exact overlaps/gaps must be verified against current MITIGATE components during design review.

security_risks.impact: Remote code execution or data exfiltration via third-party tasks
mitigations: Native assimilation only; do not load external plugins
Policy gates and signed component verification
Per-step sandboxing strategy (e.g., containers, seccomp, allowlists)

security_risks.risk: Secrets exposure in flow specs or logs
mitigations: Redact at source; use secret refs, not literals

dependency_risks.impact: Increased switching cost and operational fragility
Data loss or corruption under failover

mitigations: Human legal review of license text
Proceed only if OSI-approved and compatible
Architectural separation and clean room design

licensing.notes: No claims about ruflo licensing are made here. A human-led legal review is required prior to any adoption consideration.

strategy: Standardize on MITIGATE FlowSpec and internal executor interfaces
Abstract storage/queue and secrets behind provider-neutral adapters

principles: Preserve existing core systems and interfaces
Schema-first design with strong validation and policy gates

components.name: FlowSpec v1
components.description: Minimal, versioned JSON Schema for declarative DAGs (tasks, edges, resources, policies)
components.validation: Static validation with schema + semantic checks (acyclic, quotas, permissions)

components.name: Planner
components.description: Translates FlowSpec to executable plan with resource estimates and retry semantics
components.constraints: Idempotent planning; deterministic outputs from inputs

components.name: Coordinator
components.description: Executes plans using existing MITIGATE executor/queue with leases, heartbeats, backpressure
components.observability: Emits structured audit events, metrics, and traces

sandbox_and_validation.notes: No activation or installation of ruflo. Use synthetic FlowSpec examples and unit tests against native modules only.
test_plan: Schema validation tests for FlowSpec (positive/negative cases)
Topological sort and cycle detection tests
Retry/backoff policy tests with deterministic timing
Failure injection and recovery (lease expiry, worker crash)
Policy gate evaluations with deny/allow fixtures
adoption_gates: License verified as OSI-compatible (if any reference artifacts are used)
Security review passed (secrets handling, isolation, RBAC)
No runtime dependency on ruflo confirmed by SBOM and code review
Performance SLOs met on representative workloads
Docs and runbooks ready; feature flagged rollout plan approved

observability: Metrics: queue depth, lease expiries, retry rates
